# Claudemy for Windows

> A Windows adaptation of Claudemy (https://github.com/assafkip/claudemy, by Assaf Kipnis). Claudemy is a free, open-source Claude Code skill and an alternative to Udemy and Coursera. Give it a topic and it researches the web, compares what good sources agree on, and builds a course of 2-minute two-host audio lessons, each with a one-screen card, one small practice, and links to its sources. MIT licensed.

Install in Claude Code: `/plugin marketplace add alef-us/claudemy.win` then `/plugin install claudemy@claudemy-win`. Then ask "teach me <topic>".

Key facts:
- Output: about 12 MP3 lessons of 2 minutes, a card per lesson, a playbook of rules, and a lesson plan showing where sources disagree.
- Research: 20 to 40 web pages per topic, at most 3 per site; every lesson citation is checked against pages actually read.
- Optional: build a course from one named person's Substack or blog.
- Audio: ElevenLabs voices with an API key, or free built-in Windows voices (SAPI, through Windows PowerShell) without one.
- Requires: Claude Code with web search, Python 3 as `python`, beautifulsoup4, ffmpeg.

## Docs
- [README](https://github.com/alef-us/claudemy.win/blob/main/README.md): what it makes, how it works, install on Windows, FAQ
- [Skill instructions](https://github.com/alef-us/claudemy.win/blob/main/skills/claudemy/SKILL.md): the full step-by-step workflow Claude follows
- [Lesson example](https://github.com/alef-us/claudemy.win/blob/main/skills/claudemy/references/lesson-example.md): a complete lesson script and card
- [Article: the citation checker](https://assafkip.github.io/claudemy/blog/citation-checker.html): how the skill refuses invented sources, and what the checker does not catch
- [Original project](https://github.com/assafkip/claudemy): the macOS version this one is adapted from
